A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same P-RGE research. All 19 pages of v1 and 18 pages of v2, including appendices, equations, figures, and tables, support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning accuracy, server and edge-device runtime and memory measurements, and supplementary PEFT comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains original fine-tuning and systems experiments and additionally reports padding statistics, query-count runtime measurements, and Android memory usage.

M1.justification: Outer-loop query parallelization, inner-loop positive/negative perturbation parallelization, LoRA-FA, and the dual-forwarding ExecuTorch procedure remain unchanged. v2 Algorithm 1 formalizes the existing procedure; its Algorithm 2 matches v1 Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: The fine-tuning benchmarks and edge platforms are retained. v2's new padding analysis includes a DROP-labeled task absent from v1 (Appendix D, Figure 8), but reports no DROP fine-tuning performance.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain zero-shot, FO-Adam with full parameters or LoRA-FA, and single-query ZO with full parameters or LoRA-FA. ZO baselines are renamed MeZO. The preliminary LoRA, LoRA-FA, DoRA, and VeRA comparison is retained; newly discussed related methods are not evaluated.

E3.justification: The reported tuning protocol changes across the central experiments: LoRA alpha increases from 16 to 32, the query grid narrows from {1,2,4,8,16} to {1,4,16}, and task-dependent learning-rate grids become a shared grid. Evaluation changes from every 100 steps except SQuAD at 500 to FO every 100 and ZO every 500. Splits and iteration budgets remain unchanged; these disclosures do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds measured padding percentages for batch sizes 4 and 16 and a controlled outer-loop runtime comparison across query counts at fixed effective batch size (Appendices D–E). Separate q=4 and q=16 results also expose query sensitivity. Existing PEFT, quantization, and inner/outer-loop analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repetition counts, seed sets, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Random seeds in the algorithms concern gradient estimation rather than experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Many baseline and P-RGE scores in Tables 1–2 change, and the aggregate q>1 rows become separate q=4 and q=16 rows. For example, v1's Llama2 SQuAD F1 of 82.1 is replaced by 79.8 and 78.6 under revised tuning settings. Appendix runtime and memory results are extensively revised or expanded. v2 Table 5 adds Android memory measurements of 3.36–4.46 GB, while the existing edge runtime values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The RGE equation, SGD update, LoRA relationships, and memory/computation complexity discussion retain their mathematical substance. The new pseudocode restates the existing method; neither version provides new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 elevates ExecuTorch integration without runtime-code modifications into an explicit headline contribution and introduces headline claims of up to 4.3× end-to-end speedup and 9.87% accuracy improvement. The underlying claims about parallelization, efficient fine-tuning, and practical edge deployment already appear in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds practical query-count recommendations, a shuffling tradeoff for length-based batching, and explanations for omitted edge baselines. It removes v1 Appendix A.8's large-vocabulary logits-memory limitation and proposed tiling remedy. Its new Android–Jetson comparison in Section 4.3 contrasts TinyLlama FP16 at 15.73 seconds with Llama2 NF4 at 8.60 seconds, so the settings do not support a controlled platform comparison.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and repository link, overall P-RGE pseudocode, and clearer export-workflow and prompt-template provenance information. Hyperparameter documentation is revised, while existing prompt contents, iteration budgets, and device specifications are largely retained. Repository availability itself cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning against on-device and federated training through a dedicated discussion of FwdLLM, HETLORA, PocketLLM, and PockEngine. It also adds Sparse-MeZO, inference-framework context, and padding/shuffling references. This extends the earlier LoRA/ZO-focused treatment; the Gemma and sub-4-bit fine-tuning references are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten around resource and infrastructure challenges. Method explanations and the experimental narrative are expanded and reorganized, experimental setup moves into the main text, appendices A.1–A.9 become A–G, and method labels are revised throughout.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout, redraws the deployment workflow, restructures comparison tables, and reorganizes plots with legends and numerical annotations. It adds a padding illustration, an end-to-end runtime visualization, and a padding-statistics figure. Existing quantization results and the weight-memory table move from the appendix into the main text.

improvement.justification: Explicit query-specific results, controlled runtime and padding analyses, Android memory measurements, and clearer method documentation make v2's efficiency claims easier to assess. These provide a limited net improvement to an already demonstrated system. The benefits are tempered by removing the large-vocabulary memory caveat and introducing a model- and quantization-mismatched Android–Jetson comparison in Section 4.3.
